paper_title: Combinatorial Perpetual Scheduling: Existence and Computation of Low-Height Schedules
statement: ▶ Open Problem 1. Does there exists a polynomial-time implementation of a height-2 schedule for matroid CBGT instances when access to I is given through some natural oracle?
context: Let us call a CBGT instance (E, I, g) a matroid instance if (E, I) is a matroid. We have shown that any matroid CBGT instance has a schedule π with h(π) < 2. However, the implementation suggested by our proof uses time exponential in the number of bits required to represent g. Ideally, we would like an algorithm which is given access to I through some reasonable oracle (e.g. an indepence oracle) and which implements a schedule π with h(π) < 2 (or even d(π) < 1) in time polynomial in both |E| and the number of bits required to represent g. ▶ Open Problem 1. Does there exists a polynomial-time implementation of a height-2 schedule for matroid CBGT instances when access to I is given through some natural oracle? An independence systems (E, I) is a ℓ-system if, for any S ⊆ E, the ratio of the smallest to the largest maximal independent subset of S is at most ℓ. Examples of ℓ-systems include the set systems obtained from the intersection of ℓ matroids [34]. Moreover, matroids are exactly the 1-systems. As we have shown that the family of matroid CBGT instances admit height-2 schedules, it is natural to ask the following. ▶ Open Problem 2. Is there a function f : N → N such that all ℓ-system CBGT instances admit an f (ℓ)-height schedule?
